statement: AUDUSD movements that deviate materially from an estimated relationship with cross-asset variables, including relative interest rates, global equities and commodity (iron ore, coal, gold) prices, predict subsequent FX reversal. Unusually positive deviations predict lower subsequent AUDUSD returns, while unusually negative deviations predict higher subsequent returns. The strength and duration of this relationship may depend on the stability of the cross-asset relationship and prevailing market conditions. A deviation is defined as the difference between observed AUDUSD returns over interval t and the return estimated by a model fitted using prior observations. This residual is scaled by its trailing volatility, calculated using information available before the signal. A signal occurs when the absolute standardised residual exceeds threshold s. The initial implementation uses daily signals and a predefined holding period; alternative variables, regime definitions, scaling methods and horizons are separate areas of testing.
ledger_row: constrained flows and portfolio adjustments. Commercial payments, investment funding, portfolio rebalancing and currency hedging can create FX flow that is driven by obligations or mandates rather than short-term FX-rate attractiveness. These participants may accept current prices and transaction costs to complete their adjustments. Cross-asset returns provide observable measures of repricing; they do not directly identify the underlying flows.
mechanism: cross-asset repricing changes investors’ desired asset exposures and currency hedges; where a delay in reaction is expected because of the difference in open trading hour. For example, after a large down move in US equities, an Australian pension fund may want to rebalance their currency hedging by selling AUD. The resulting FX transactions may temporarily push AUDUSD beyond the movement explained by related markets, particularly when demand for immediacy exceeds available liquidity. As this pressure subsides and liquidity providers adjust their inventories, part of the excess FX movement may reverse.
evidence_standard: the edge must 1) survive 12 years of in-sample and 3 years out of sample data 2) require at least 400 samples 3) produce positive net of costs expected profit with 95% block-bootstrap confidence interval excluding 0 4) Holm family wise error rate below 0.05 5) fade position must beat a random direction control
trial_budget: no trial budget is given for the central hypothesis, as each component will be divided into further hypotheses with its own trial budget
kill_condition: if none of the trials, including baseline, pass the corrected significance threshold, or if the edge net of cost does not survive any trial
